targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/interests/events-and-festivals/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore Carnival and New Year tours through Brazil, Argentina and Peru"
lead: >-
  In the Brazil, Argentina and Peru selection, the main festive experience takes place in Rio de Janeiro. We offer itineraries for Carnival, the Champions' Parade and New Year, followed by Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and Machu Picchu. All the relevant ready-made programs also visit Chile and Bolivia. Compare the festive evenings and discover how to prepare for a long itinerary and booking.
---

## Brazil, Argentina and Peru: which celebration defines your trip?

In this combination, **the celebration takes place in Brazil, while Argentina and Peru come later in the journey**. Carnival night and New Year celebrations in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) are tied to specific calendar dates. Choose the event first, then check whether the route through the waterfalls, Buenos Aires and Peruvian monuments works for those dates.

The current catalog includes itineraries through five main countries: [Brazil](/brazil/), [Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and [Peru](/peru/). All five are part of the itinerary, although this filter highlights three. Visiting only the three named countries would require a different sequence of flights and transfers; a ready-made five-country journey cannot automatically be shortened.

If the sole purpose of your trip is a few days at Carnival, start by comparing [festival and event trips](/interests/events-and-festivals/) and [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/). If you also want Iguazu and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the longer route offers a very different experience.

## Carnival, the Champions' Parade or New Year in Rio

**Carnival and the Champions' Parade are two different events at the Sambadrome.** During the principal competitive nights, samba schools present performances used to select the winners. After the results are announced, the leading schools perform in the Champions' Parade. New Year's Eve on Rio's coast is a separate celebration, unrelated to the samba-school competition.

The catalog offers three distinct options:

| Ready-made tour | Main event |
|---|---|
| [18 days, Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | A selected evening of the Champions' Parade |
| [19 days, Carnival](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Carnival program in Rio |
| [19 days, New Year](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | New Year celebrations in Rio |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god}}

For a calendar reference, parade organizer LIESA lists February 7, 8 and 9, 2027, for the competitive performances and February 13 for the Champions' Parade. **A tour name matching the event does not itself confirm availability for those dates.** The precise departure, admission tickets, Sambadrome sector and transport after the overnight program must be checked against the chosen product's terms.

A Carnival evening may mean spending most of the night on your feet or in a noisy crowd. Sleep, the next day's excursion start time, hotel departure and the actual flight are therefore particularly important. The New Year program follows a different sequence: December 31 includes Corcovado and the festive evening, while January 1 features Sugarloaf Mountain. Allowing time to rest is what separates a comfortable festival itinerary from an exhausting race between attractions.

## Brazil after the celebration: Iguazu as a nature interlude

After Rio, the programs continue toward [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Here, the festival atmosphere gives way to a national park. Viewpoints on the Brazilian side provide a broad panorama of the cascades, while the Argentine side offers different walking routes and perspectives.

**The two sides of Iguazu are in different countries.** Crossing to [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) takes documents and time for border procedures. Plan the waterfall visit around weather, excursion duration and any evening flight. Following a busy night in Rio, it makes little sense to overload this day with further optional trips.

The Brazilian portion does not end automatically after the festival performance. The number of nights at Iguazu determines whether both sides can be explored without rushing onward.

## Argentina: the end of the festive stage and the start of a city itinerary

From the Iguazu area, travelers head to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The program includes the capital's neighborhoods and an evening tango show. Tango has a different role from Carnival samba: it is a separate stage tradition and cultural excursion, not a second main festival event.

Buenos Aires is a natural stop between the Iguazu nature stage and later flights. Check how much time remains for an independent city walk and how much is taken by transfers, scheduled excursions and the journey to the airport.

After Argentina, the selected five-country programs fly to Santiago, then travel through the Atacama Desert and Bolivia toward Peru. Their schedule does not contain a direct Buenos Aires–Machu Picchu flight: **[Chile and Bolivia](/multi-country/bolivia_chile/) are real stages of the journey**. Removing them would require recalculating all logistics and pricing rather than simply deleting their names from the excursion list.

## Peru: reaching Machu Picchu on a festival-based schedule

Peru completes the long route after the high-altitude days in Bolivia. The itineraries include the journey to [Lake Titicaca and Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), then [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and Machu Picchu.

The key planning question is: **which Machu Picchu ticket is available on the date determined by Carnival or New Year?** Entry follows specified circuits and times. A ticket for another date is not an equivalent replacement if a flight from Cusco to Lima is already scheduled. When booking the entire trip, coordinate the circuit, excursion duration, train to the site and return time.

Southern Hemisphere summer feels different in Rio and the Andes. Brazil is hot and humid, while January and February fall in the rainy season around Cusco. Road delays and wet conditions on open trails are possible even when the earlier city celebrations enjoyed perfect weather.

The appeal lies in combining a major event with archaeology, but the trip demands considerable travel time. To choose the season for Machu Picchu more freely, compare [Peru itineraries](/peru/tour/) and [culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Flights, money and documents after the celebrations

On these journeys, international and domestic flights alternate with overland crossings. Before paying, check not only airport names but also onward departure times, how tickets are issued and whether luggage must be collected during connections. A delayed flight after a fixed festival date can affect excursions in the next country.

Russian citizens should check short-stay tourism and passport requirements before departure for **Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru**, including transit and re-entry if ticketing changes. Other nationalities may need different documents. If changing airlines or routing via a third country, check the particular airport's and ticket's transit conditions too.

Currencies also change: Brazil uses the real, Argentina and Chile have their respective pesos, Bolivia the boliviano, and Peru the sol. There is no universal guarantee that US dollars or payment cards will be accepted. Travelers departing from Russia should confirm whether their particular payment methods work, understand exchange options and keep a cash reserve. ATM access in a city should not be assumed on the high-altitude section.

Pack for tropical heat alongside a light rain jacket, insulating layers and comfortable footwear for steps and uneven paths. Cabin baggage allowances on domestic flights may differ from those of the intercontinental journey. We help coordinate the route, transfers and preparation for changing climates; exact included services and tickets are determined by the selected itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about a Carnival trip through Brazil, Argentina and Peru

### Can we experience Carnival and Machu Picchu on one trip?

Yes. Suitable five-country itineraries begin with festivities in Rio and end in Peru. Argentina, Chile and Bolivia lie between, so allow time for the complete route.

### How does a regular Carnival evening differ from the Champions' Parade?

Competitive parades take place before the winners are announced; the Champions' Parade follows the results. The dates differ, so check the specific ticket and evening against the tour terms.

### Is there a tour limited to these three countries in the catalog?

The selection includes tours featuring Brazil, Argentina and Peru as main destinations, but the current offers also pass through Chile and Bolivia. A three-country journey would require a custom program.

### When should Machu Picchu be booked if the journey is tied to Carnival?

Before finalizing the itinerary. Entry is linked to a date, time and selected circuit within the complex, so it must be coordinated with flights and train arrangements.

kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore the food and wine of Argentina, Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  On a route through Argentina, Brazil and Peru, food experiences are distributed unevenly.
  Buenos Aires includes a tango show with dinner; Rio and Iguazu focus on sightseeing;
  and Peru involves a journey through Cusco to Machu Picchu. A separate wine tasting
  is offered in the Maipo Valley, during the Chilean stage of the larger journey.
---

## Combining food experiences and three countries on one trip

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining **Argentina, Brazil and Peru** in a multi-country itinerary labeled “Food and Wine.” This filter needs to be interpreted correctly: the theme applies to **the whole tour**, not a promise that tastings and cooking workshops are included in each of the three countries.

On the current [20-day journey through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), travelers visit Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The clearest food experience **within the three selected countries** is an evening tango show with dinner in the Argentine capital. A specialist wine excursion is offered as an option in Chile. You may choose local restaurants during free time elsewhere, but those plans should not be presented as an already paid culinary tour.

To compare routes without a thematic filter, see [itineraries through Argentina, Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/). If wineries and tastings are your main goal, also explore the [multi-country food and wine catalog](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Argentina: Buenos Aires, tango and dinner

After the Argentine side of Iguazu, travelers arrive in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). A city tour of historic and contemporary neighborhoods is scheduled, followed in the evening by a [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/). The evening's menu includes traditional dishes and Argentine wines.

This combines cuisine and culture in a meaningful way: dinner accompanies a dance performance rather than a separate asado cooking class or a professional wine tasting. Visitors wanting to study gastronomy in depth should distinguish these formats before choosing a trip.

The route covers La Boca, San Telmo, Puerto Madero and other parts of the capital. During free time, you can independently select a café or restaurant to suit your preferences and budget. But **no particular restaurant, dishes, reservation time or paid food guide is specified in the standard program**.

Pace matters here too: the sightseeing day and evening show are followed by a trip to Montevideo and then a flight to Chile. Any spare window for an additional food experience must be coordinated with real travel arrangements.

## Brazil: Rio, Iguazu and time for your own discoveries

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the program focuses on Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and city panoramas. At [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the main experiences are waterfall excursions. These are full days exploring Brazil, but the included services **do not contain a separate food-market tour or cooking workshop**.

Brazilian dishes can be a self-directed part of the journey between excursions. Decide in advance whether you simply want to try local food at regular lunches and dinners or need a dedicated culinary itinerary including specific venues, a meeting with a chef or a tasting. The latter requires a separately arranged program; Rio's presence on the route does not itself promise these services.

At Iguazu, check the timing of transfers and both waterfall visits. Busy days crossing between Brazilian and Argentine sides may leave less free time than a relaxed stay in one city.

## Peru: Cusco, Machu Picchu and food alongside a high-altitude itinerary

In Peru, the journey runs through the Lake Titicaca area, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima. These stages include travel, archaeological excursions, rail transport and Inca monuments. The published itinerary does not specify cooking sessions with a set menu, tasting menus or culinary-school visits.

For travelers interested in Peruvian cuisine, this is more **an opportunity to add your own restaurant plans** than a ready-made culinary product. In particular, avoid scheduling a long late dinner before an early departure to an archaeological site or between lengthy high-altitude transfers. Elevation changes and the allocation of overnight stays affect well-being and appetite, so maintain a comfortable pace, keep drinking water available and allow time to rest.

In Lima, sightseeing includes urban neighborhoods and the historic center. If a dedicated food day is important, arrange it when deciding the trip's format and duration rather than assuming a standard city tour automatically includes restaurants.

## Why the wine theme appears here: Maipo Valley

The key distinction for this country combination is that **the specialist wine excursion takes place in Chile, a fourth country on the larger itinerary**, even though the page filters by Argentina, Brazil and Peru. During the Santiago stop, an optional [Maipo Valley winery tour](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) with tasting is offered. This is a paid option available subject to a minimum number of participants.

It is a separate product and requires a separate booking decision. If wine tasting is a must-have, confirm the excursion, its timing relative to sightseeing in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the terms for participants well in advance. Without this option, the route remains a cultural sightseeing tour with dinner at the tango show.

The same approach helps when comparing other themed trips: examine where each tasting actually occurs, whether it is included or optional, and the day's demands, not merely the country names or the word “wine.”

## What is actually included in the food-related experiences

| Stage | Actual format |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Tango show with dinner |
| Rio and Iguazu | Sightseeing; meals according to the itinerary |
| Cusco and Lima | Cultural journey; no dedicated food tour |
| Maipo Valley, Chile | Optional wine excursion |

The 20-day tour includes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, overland transfers, scheduled excursions and meals specified by day. Drinks, lunches or dinners not included in the description should not be treated as prepaid. Departure dates and accommodation details are provided on the current tour page.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

## Choosing a multi-country culinary journey

Start with your primary goal. If you value **a balance of culture and food**, a sightseeing itinerary through the three countries with a tango dinner may suit your interests. If professional tastings, vineyards, markets and cooking activities matter most, compare [Argentina food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/) and the [general Ada Tours food and wine theme](/interests/food-and-wine/), then confirm the exact program.

Border crossings and domestic flights also require attention. The longer route includes Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia, so flights and free evenings cannot be assessed using only the three selected countries. If you plan to carry drinks or food products across borders, check customs restrictions separately by nationality, itinerary and departure date; there is no single universal rule for all six countries.

## Frequently asked questions about food in Argentina, Brazil and Peru

### Does the itinerary include a wine tasting?

A tasting is offered as an optional excursion to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/maipo-valley/), during the Chile stage. No separate wine tasting is specified among the mandatory activities in the three selected countries.

### Is dinner at the tango show included?

Yes. The [tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/) is included in the published 20-day itinerary. Check the exact menu and drinks against the terms of the selected evening.

### Is there a Peruvian cooking class?

No such activity appears in the published program. The Peru stage focuses on Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima. Separate culinary experiences must be arranged as additions.

### Can we visit only Argentina, Brazil and Peru?

The current ready-made itinerary includes six countries. A journey strictly limited to three would require selecting or arranging another route while keeping the food experiences that matter to you.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore nature tours in Argentina, Brazil and Peru"
lead: >-
  Brazil, Argentina and Peru bring together Iguazu Falls and the high-altitude landscapes of Cusco and Titicaca, with Patagonian glaciers added on some itineraries. Choosing the actual tour matters: a 14-day route runs from Rio and Iguazu to Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca, while a different 15-day group tour adds El Calafate and Perito Moreno Glacier. Similar countries do not guarantee the same nature program.
---

## Nature in Brazil, Argentina and Peru: two different journeys

Our themed selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. You can focus on the waterfalls and Andes or choose a more extensive journey including Argentine Patagonia. The decisive differences lie in itinerary details, not the list of three countries.

For example, [“Brazil, Argentina and Peru in 14 Days”](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) connects Rio de Janeiro, both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca. The [15-day “Brazil, Peru and Argentina” group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) also travels to El Calafate and Perito Moreno after visiting sites in Brazil and Peru.

| Main interest | What to check |
|---|---|
| Iguazu Falls | Which sides of the border are visited |
| Andes and Machu Picchu | Days in Cusco and the Sacred Valley |
| Lake Titicaca | Whether Puno is included |
| Patagonian glaciers | Whether El Calafate is on the route |

## Brazil: Rio and panoramic views of Iguazu

In Brazil, the natural setting often first reveals itself in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), where the ocean, granite hills and the city meet. Yet the major nature highlight of many journeys is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/).

On the Brazilian side, travelers see the wide front of the waterfalls and surrounding forest. Subtropical vegetation is part of the protected natural area, and spray and humidity are part of the experience. Panoramic viewpoints are ideal for photographing the cascades, but protect your phone and camera from water.

Many tours in this combination also include [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina. The Argentine side brings visitors closer to individual stretches of the falls from different directions. Visiting both banks depends on schedules, trail conditions and applicable border-crossing rules.

For more options, see [Brazil nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/), but on a combined three-country itinerary, checking the precise Iguazu days is more important.

## Peru: Machu Picchu, Cusco and Lake Titicaca

On the 14-day itinerary, the Peru stage starts in Lima and continues to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The change from a coastal city to high-altitude districts can noticeably affect both climate and how travelers feel.

Machu Picchu stands among steep mountain slopes at approximately 2,430 meters. UNESCO recognizes the sanctuary as a combination of exceptional Inca architecture and the rich natural environment of the eastern Andes. Terraces, stone walls and clouds above wooded mountains form one landscape. However, an ordinary visit to the site does not automatically include the multi-day Inca Trail.

Lake Titicaca offers a completely different view: an open high-altitude expanse of water and nearby communities. The 14-day itinerary names Uros and Taquile. On the [15-day group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), Peru focuses on Lima, Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu, without Titicaca in the stated main route. That is a significant difference despite the similar durations.

## Argentina: Iguazu or also Perito Moreno Glacier?

The Argentine portion of this combination may involve only Buenos Aires and the Argentine side of Iguazu, or it may extend to Patagonia. The 14-day itinerary does not include El Calafate but does include Titicaca in Peru.

On the 15-day group program, after the Peru stage, travelers fly to Buenos Aires and continue to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) for [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). The ice mass, cold lake and Patagonian wind contrast sharply with tropical Iguazu. A warm layer is necessary even after hot days in Brazil.

**Checking whether El Calafate appears on the itinerary is the best way to establish whether the glacier stage is included.** Patagonia should not be assumed to be a guaranteed feature of every tour through Argentina, Brazil and Peru.

## Choosing an itinerary for weather and activity levels

These three countries involve travel between humid Iguazu, the high Andes and, on some trips, cold Patagonia. One set of clothes will not suit every day. Bring light items for the waterfalls, warm layers and closed shoes for high-altitude cities, and wind protection if Patagonia is included.

The **sequence of altitude gain** matters too. After Rio and Iguazu, a traveler may arrive in Cusco; the pace of the first mountain days should reflect how they feel. For individual medical risks, discuss high-altitude travel with a doctor. Allow contingency time for ground transfers and weather-related delays when planning flights.

Do not compare two itineraries solely by their length: the 14-day tour includes Titicaca, while the 15-day group tour includes Perito Moreno. The latter is designed for 10–20 participants and 4-star hotels with breakfast; these conditions cannot be assumed for other tours. Prices may also be calculated on different bases, so compare them only after checking services and accommodation.

Find more options in the [full Argentina, Brazil and Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/). For journeys emphasizing high-altitude landscapes, explore the [“Nature” theme](/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Brazil and Peru

### Does every tour include Perito Moreno Glacier?

No. It is included, for example, on the 15-day group itinerary visiting El Calafate. The “Brazil, Argentina and Peru in 14 Days” itinerary does not include that stage.

### Can we see both sides of Iguazu?

Several current itineraries include the Brazilian and Argentine sides. Check the allocated days and border-crossing conditions for the actual travel dates.

### Is Lake Titicaca included on every Peru itinerary?

No. The 14-day program includes Uros and Taquile on Titicaca, while the specified 15-day group itinerary focuses on Cusco and Machu Picchu in Peru.

### Can Machu Picchu and Patagonia be combined on one trip?

Yes. The 15-day group tour including Machu Picchu and Perito Moreno is one example. Consider flight frequency, altitude, changing weather and physical demands.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/interests/wildlife/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Where wildlife watching is scheduled on the full itinerary"
lead: >-
  The “Wildlife and Safaris” filter for Argentina, Brazil and Peru shows a longer 32-day journey in which the genuine opportunity to observe island wildlife takes place in the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. Iguazu and the Andes in the three selected countries are nature stops; shorter programs without a wildlife theme can be compared separately under “Nature.”
---

## Where wildlife watching occurs on the journey through Argentina, Brazil and Peru

This wildlife catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [a 32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). In Brazil and Argentina, the route visits Iguazu Falls; in Peru, the Andes, Titicaca and Machu Picchu. But the reason for the “Wildlife and Safaris” designation is the opportunity for marine wildlife sightings during outings in the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, outside the three selected countries.

This should be distinguished from a specialist safari. The “Wildlife and Safaris” theme refers to the full itinerary; it does not guarantee sightings of rare species in every selected country. When choosing, examine the actual excursions, duration of nature stops and whether a bird park or forest outing is included or optional.

## Iguazu: one natural complex and two different experiences

[Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is a starting point for broad waterfall panoramas. [On the Argentine side near Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), trails and walkways approach the cascades and river from other directions. UNESCO describes both protected parks as important parts of the Atlantic region's subtropical forests, with high plant and animal diversity.

On a separate [14-day nature and culture tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), which is outside this wildlife filter, two days are devoted to the waterfalls: first Brazil, then Argentina and a flight to Buenos Aires. Visitors can compare viewpoints and walking routes, but that does not guarantee seeing a jaguar, tapir or another elusive species.

On the [15-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), travelers visit the Brazilian side of the falls. [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is offered as an optional excursion, not automatically included wildlife watching on the main route. Similarly, on the longer [20-day six-country trip](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), the bird park and Macuco Safari are listed as separate opportunities with their own terms.

## Argentina: from subtropical forest to a Patagonian glacier

For Argentina's nature stages, it is important to compare **the precise locations visited**. On the 14-day itinerary, Argentina mainly means Iguazu and Buenos Aires. The [15-day group trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) adds El Calafate and an excursion to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/).

Perito Moreno offers a different landscape: glacier, mountain lake and Patagonian weather instead of humid subtropical forest. Choose this stage if contrasting scenery and seeing a glacier are priorities. The presence of Perito Moreno, however, does not automatically mean marine wildlife, whales, penguins or dedicated birdwatching; those activities are not included on the named days.

Changing regions adds flights and requires different luggage. At Iguazu, bring light clothes and rain protection; in Patagonia, windproof, water-resistant outerwear and warm layers are useful.

## Peru: Andean highlands, Titicaca and mountain forests

The Peru stage includes [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), Machu Picchu and, on some programs, [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu lies on the eastern slopes of the Andes, where highlands give way to moist mountain forests. UNESCO recognizes the area's natural value alongside its Inca monuments.

On the [14-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/), the Cusco–Puno road crosses high-altitude plains where herds of llamas and alpacas may be seen. A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) is scheduled, but its main focus is local culture, not wildlife watching. On the 15-day tour, the Peruvian stage concentrates on the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu without the same journey to Titicaca.

If watching particular birds or animals is your primary aim, choose according to specific nature excursions rather than simply the destination Peru and the tour's general theme.

## Other itineraries for natural scenery

| Tour without the wildlife designation | Main nature highlight |
|---|---|
| [14 days, three countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) | Both sides of Iguazu, Andes and Titicaca |
| [15 days, three countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) | Iguazu and Perito Moreno Glacier |
| [18 days, five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Iguazu, then Atacama, Uyuni and the Andes |

The three tours above carry the “Nature” theme but are not part of the wildlife selection. They have their own [nature travel catalog for Argentina, Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_peru/interests/nature/). The tour below carries the “Wildlife and Safaris” designation, with possible sightings of island fauna during its Galápagos stage. On multi-country tours, wildlife experiences may take place outside the countries named in the selection, so check the full itinerary and actual days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The third alternative also passes through Chile and Bolivia. Their high-altitude lagoons, desert and salt flats add nature experiences but require several additional countries and a different pace. It would be inaccurate to call it a trip exclusively through Argentina, Brazil and Peru.

To compare a wider range, see [multi-country wildlife-watching trips](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). For Brazilian waterfalls, forests and landscapes, see the separate [Brazil nature catalog](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/).

## Time for nature, weather and limitations

**At Iguazu**, allow sufficient hours in the park, time to travel between sides of the border and the possibility of weather-related restrictions on individual trails. The time required for border formalities depends on the group's documents and the day.

**In Peru**, altitude is a major consideration: Cusco is at approximately 3,350 meters, and the Titicaca area is higher. After low-elevation stops, travelers need time to acclimatize. Plan the pace, physical demands and any medical limitations in advance, especially if children or older participants are traveling.

**In Patagonia**, when included, additional warm clothing is needed. City walks, boat excursions and specialist nature outings have different terms. A glacier excursion does not confirm that additional trekking or a cruise is included in the price.

Ada Tours helps coordinate flights, transfers, parks and visiting days within the specific itinerary. Entry requirements depend on the traveler's nationality; payment methods and bank card acceptance depend on the country and card issuer, without universal guarantees.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife and nature alternatives

### Will we see animals at Iguazu Falls?

The Iguazu region supports diverse wildlife, but encounters in the wild are not guaranteed. Check which park walks are included in the selected itinerary. For a more focused introduction to birds, see whether [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is included or available only for an extra charge.

### Which itinerary should we choose for Perito Moreno Glacier?

Among the nature-focused alternatives, the glacier is included in the [15-day group trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), which does not have the wildlife designation. The [14-day route](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) allocates the Argentine days differently and does not reach El Calafate.

### Can Iguazu and the Andes be combined without additional countries?

Yes. The [14-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) travels through Brazil, Argentina and Peru, combining Iguazu with Cusco and Titicaca. Longer options add Chile, Bolivia and other countries, making them different journeys.

### Is Machu Picchu a nature or history excursion?

Both dimensions matter at the sanctuary, but a standard tour chiefly explores Inca monuments. Specialist birdwatching or wildlife activities must be explicitly listed in the itinerary.

## Four countries from the Atlantic to the Andes: which itinerary is offered?

[Brazil](/brazil/), [Argentina](/argentina/), [Uruguay](/uruguay/) and [Peru](/peru/) may look like a complete combination in their own right: tropical Rio, waterfalls, cities along the Río de la Plata and Inca archaeological monuments. But our current programs include these places within longer journeys rather than visiting only four countries in sequence.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [20-day six-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) ends in Lima after Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) follows a similar opening sequence before continuing after Peru to Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia. All four countries named in this selection are main destinations on both itineraries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The actual sequence matters when judging costs and a comfortable travel pace. For example, the journey between [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is a ferry excursion, while reaching Peru involves high-altitude regions of other countries.

## Both sides of Iguazu: one natural system, two borders

The Brazil stage starts in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and city sightseeing. A flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) follows. Travelers visit the waterfalls from the Brazilian side and, on a different itinerary day, the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

For travelers, these are not duplicate visits. The Brazilian viewpoints provide broad panoramas, while trails on the Argentine side bring visitors closer to cascades from other angles. But behind the different views lies an **international border**. Crossing time, park admission, documentation and tickets all require separate arrangements.

After the Argentine excursion, the journey continues by air to Buenos Aires. Additional activities at the falls should not automatically be regarded as included or scheduled before a flight without extra time. Compare [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [Argentina itineraries](/argentina/tour/) for separate excursions, but the terms of each product depend on its own program.

## Argentina and Uruguay: Montevideo as a day trip

In Buenos Aires, the itinerary combines a city sightseeing excursion with an evening tango program. An early transfer to the port and a ferry to Montevideo follow. Visitors explore Uruguay's capital and return to Argentina.

This section lets travelers compare two cities on the Río de la Plata without changing their main overnight base. Check how much free time is available, the ferry departure point and boarding requirements for the return. **Montevideo is included, but Uruguay's coastline and a multi-day stay in the country are not.**

Crossing an international border twice in one day has implications for documents. Even where simplified entry applies to a nationality, passport validity, traveler status, possible re-entry into Argentina and carrier requirements still need checking.

## Why Chile and Bolivia lie between Buenos Aires and Peru

After returning from Uruguay, travelers fly from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The route continues through Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), where a two-day Bolivian off-road section begins. It passes high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). From Uyuni, the group flies to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and, after Tiwanaku, crosses into Peru by land.

This explains why the country names in the catalog heading are not a ready-made flight itinerary of “Brazil–Argentina–Uruguay–Peru.” Chile and Bolivia add more than sightseeing. In the actual product, they form the route connecting the Atlantic-side capitals with the Peruvian Andes.

If you want only those four countries, we can discuss a custom trip, but direct or connecting flights, the duration of the Peru stage and pricing must be planned anew. The ready-made 20-day itinerary does not automatically become a four-country tour.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima

After crossing the Bolivia–Peru land border, the itinerary heads to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Travelers visit [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and other heritage sites in Cusco. A flight then brings them to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), with Miraflores and the historic center.

Machu Picchu must be treated as a distinct scheduling requirement. Official admission is tied to a specific circuit, date and time. With several countries already visited before Cusco, contingency time after international travel is especially helpful. Do not assume that admission can be chosen at the last minute regardless of ticket availability.

Altitude is another major factor. Rio, Buenos Aires and Montevideo are much lower than parts of the Bolivian Altiplano and Cusco. Travelers need time to adjust, and those with chronic illnesses should consult a doctor before confirming a high-altitude itinerary. Numerous urban excursions do not mean that physical demands are the same across all stages.

## Climate and luggage: humid tropics, cities and cold Andean nights

One “summer suitcase” will not suit this combination. Rio and Iguazu can bring heat, humidity and rain; Buenos Aires and Montevideo call for city clothing and wind protection near the water. On the Chilean–Bolivian high-altitude section, nights may be cold, winds strong and solar radiation intense even in cool air. In Peru, [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and Cusco also have different climates.

| Stage | What to pack |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Light clothes, rain protection |
| Buenos Aires and Montevideo | Comfortable shoes, wind layer |
| Atacama and Uyuni | Warm layers, sun protection |
| Cusco and Machu Picchu | Shoes with good grip, rain jacket |

A versatile layered wardrobe is often more practical than a heavy suitcase full of incompatible outfits. Nevertheless, check actual domestic-flight baggage allowances with each airline. Weight and size limits may differ from an intercontinental flight.

## Visas, currencies and budget with repeated entries

Brazil uses the **real (BRL)**, Argentina the **peso (ARS)**, Uruguay the **peso (UYU)** and Peru the **sol (PEN)**. The full journey also involves Chilean pesos and bolivianos. Choosing cash solely for the four countries in the heading would be a mistake because spending also occurs in the additional countries.

Separate the overall program cost from personal expenses such as meals not included, souvenirs, optional excursions and small purchases. Not every stage requires exchanging a large amount: personal spending on a one-day Montevideo trip differs from a multi-day stay in Peru. International card acceptance, fees and ATM availability depend on the bank and location. Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards do not work outside Russia through those networks.

Check entry rules by nationality and travel date **for all six or eight countries** actually visited, including connections. Pay particular attention to repeated entries into Argentina around Iguazu and after Uruguay. At high-altitude land border crossings, confirm operating hours and transport requirements. We help organize the checks and arrange transport, but border authorities make entry decisions.

## Who should choose 20 days and who should choose 32?

Both options share an extensive section through the four named countries, as well as Chile and Bolivia. The longer trip differs because **Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia come after Peru**. This extends the itinerary north through South America, not by adding another week on beaches in Brazil or Uruguay.

If your main priorities are Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Machu Picchu, the 20-day itinerary covers that sequence without an Ecuador–Colombia continuation. If you want to experience more natural areas and cities of the continent, explore the 32-day option. Compare actual accommodation, group excursions and included flights on both tour pages: neither a country's size nor a trip's duration replaces the detailed program.

## Frequently asked questions about a journey through four countries

### Will we see both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu?

Yes, both current itineraries include visits on the two sides of the border. These are different excursion days with separate access and transport arrangements.

### Can we spend several days in Uruguay?

The ready-made program treats Montevideo as a day trip from Buenos Aires. A longer stay and coastal visit would require changing the itinerary.

### Do these tours include a direct flight from Uruguay to Peru?

No. After Montevideo, travelers return to Buenos Aires, then proceed through Chile and Bolivia before entering Peru overland from Bolivia.

### Where are altitude changes hardest to handle?

On the Chile–Bolivia section and subsequent journeys through the Andes. Adaptation is individual, and travel insurance should be checked for high-altitude excursions and planned activities.

### Why are six- and eight-country tours shown if I select four countries?

Because the static selection finds itineraries containing all the countries specified. It shows relevant larger routes, not a promise of a product limited to four countries.
